family_meta.description: European bat species classifier for ultrasonic recordings: 21 species plus a Background class, from a log-mel spectrogram of 384 kHz audio. Six independently trained checkpoints are published for ensemble use; one also works on its own.
family_meta.author: bsg-bat team

requirements_note: requirements.min_ram_mb is a conservative, high-biased RAM floor: measured peak RSS + 15% where a benchmark exists, else a size-derived estimate biased high (a too-low floor risks OOM; a too-high floor only over-excludes on the smallest devices). Measured values will replace the estimates over time.
naming: legacy names, frozen; new files follow <family>-<upstream>[-<region>]-<variant>-b<build>.<ext>

ensemble.note: independently trained checkpoints with identical graph, I/O and labels; the upstream authors combine the per-class logits or probabilities with min, max, mean or median. A single checkpoint also works on its own. Six sessions in one process peak at about 700 to 730 MB RSS (one session 200 to 240 MB); set session.intra_op.allow_spinning to 0 or share a thread pool, otherwise per-session pools spin against each other at several threads (see docs/bsg-bat.md).

notes: Faithful ONNX conversion of BSG-BAT v0.21 (CC-BY-4.0), PyTorch vs ONNX Runtime max absolute difference below 3e-6 per checkpoint. Not a waveform model: the caller builds the spectrogram described in `frontend`. Selection lists the single r1 checkpoint; the six-member ensemble takes about six times the time of one session (with intra-op spinning disabled when several threads are used) and about 700 to 730 MB RSS against 200 to 240 MB for one. Only the onnxruntime-cpu backend was tested, so no other backend is listed.

input.name: spectrogram
input.note: normalized log10 mel spectrogram of 384 kHz mono audio: 512 time frames (about 1.024 s) by 128 mel bins, 1 channel. Not a waveform.

outputs.name: logits
outputs.note: multi-label: probability = 1 / (1 + exp(-logit)) per class; class order is bsgbat_labels.txt (21 species, then Background as index 21)

frontend.mel: librosa melspectrogram defaults (power 2, Slaney scale and norm)
frontend.normalize: per 512-frame segment: z-score over the whole segment (population std), subtract the per-mel-bin median, clip to [0, 6]
frontend.segments: for S mel frames (librosa centered framing) the reference makes max(ceil((S - 512) / 250), 1) segments, segment i starting at frame 250 * i; the frames after the last segment's end (up to 250) are not scored; a recording shorter than 512 frames is zero padded in the power spectrogram before the log and yields one segment
frontend.note: content above the source Nyquist is absent after resampling, and the model reads 9-150 kHz, so the source must be ultrasonic (a 48 kHz recording cannot work). Lossy codecs discard the ultrasonic content.
